record.file_problem: The text contains repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and linked output files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: Applies a weight-space edit based on a refusal direction and reports refusal outcomes, testing practical removal by a method different from the original activation ablation.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal and KL outcomes for Heretic-edited models. It also describes residual alignment after abliteration. The trial count and search process are described, but settings used to choose directions or per-layer weights are not separate findings here. Conversion instructions, speed, and hardware notes do not bear on the claim.
record.test_reason: The repo applies a refusal-direction weight edit (Heretic abliteration) to a newly released model, Gemma 4 12B-it. It reports refusals on 100 harmful prompts before (99/100) and after (37/100 by keyword count, 3 explicit refusals), which bears directly on V2 in a new setting. It does not test activation ablation or adding the direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it omits a key qualification. The README reports that Heretic abliteration of Gemma 4 12B-it cut keyword-counted refusals from 99/100 to 37/100, of which only 3 were explicit refusals. It keeps KL at 0.0397 and calls ordinary-prompt quality essentially unchanged. After the edit, harmful prompts' alignment with the direction drops to match harmless prompts.
record.recipe_differences: Heretic edits attn.o_proj and mlp.down_proj weights using a rank-3, norm-preserving LoRA merged on save, with per-layer weights selected by search; it does not perform the original activation projection at every layer and position or test adding the direction. This is a tool/application repo, not a replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports different refusal/KL tradeoffs across trials 143, 114, and 92. It also states that the evaluation uses a keyword count and a maximum response length of 200.
record.problems: Evidence is limited to README-reported results for one model. The refusal measure is a keyword count, and the README says most of trial 143's 37 counts were not explicit refusals. Ordinary-prompt quality is described as essentially unchanged, but no direct capability benchmark or uncertainty estimates are provided.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcome-bearing trial results were omitted. Search settings and trial counts are not separate behavioural results; conversion, speed, and hardware outcomes do not bear on the claim.

untested.parts: Activation-space directional ablation at every layer and position, inducing refusal by adding the direction, and capability benchmarks. The weight edit uses searched per-layer strengths, not the V1 intervention.

Other released models and editing procedures, a direct capability benchmark (only KL and an unread qualitative comparison), and refusal with Gemma 4's thinking mode enabled. The README's usage instructions turn thinking off; the evaluation setting for thinking mode is not stated.

missing.what: Explicit refusals after the edit: 3/100 for trial 143, versus 37/100 by keyword count.
missing.locator: README, text below the results table

missing.what: Qualitative comparison of ordinary-prompt quality between the original and edited models.
Numeric per-layer alignment before and after the edit (peak 0.46 near layer 30).

record.verdict_notes: This is a hobbyist tool repo, not peer reviewed, and only the README was read. The original paper also used weight orthogonalization, so this is the same kind of method in a new model (T3), not a different method. All trials apart from 143's re-evaluation report search-phase scores. The refusal measure is Heretic's keyword count, which overstates refusals. No uncertainty estimates are given.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests, activation projection at every layer and position, or general capabilities with a direct capability benchmark.
Tests one Gemma 4 instruct model and one Heretic weight-edit procedure; does not establish the result across released models generally.

relation.reason: Its own before/after refusal counts (99/100 -> 37/100, 3 explicit) bear directly on whether a weight edit removes refusal in a released model.

tranche.reason: It applies a refusal-direction weight edit (Heretic: rank-3 norm-preserving LoRA on attn.o_proj and mlp.down_proj, searched per layer) to a new released model, Gemma 4 12B-it, and reports refusal counts before and after. That is a new setting with a result on V2. T2 is also defensible because the recipe differs from the original.

source_check.notes: The pack gives no [lN] ids for its verdicts, so l1 and l2 are positional: l1 is the supports verdict, l2 the limits_scope one. The '3 explicit refusals' figure and the claim that 'ordinary-prompt quality is essentially unchanged' rest on files not in the text (outputs/eval/compare.md, heretic.json). There is no capability benchmark, and the layer-alignment result (peak 0.46 near layer 30) appears only in figure alt text.

statements.correction: Trial 143: 99/100 -> 37/100 keyword-counted refusals (re-evaluated; 35/100 in the search), KL 0.0397. README: only 3 of the 37 were explicit refusals; the rest mention words like 'illegal'. Trials 114 (45/100, KL 0.0293) and 92 (61/100, KL 0.0190) are gentler search-phase Pareto-front trials. Record verdict for trial 143: V2 supports; limits_scope applies only to trials 114 and 92.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but filing gh:szarn as 'incomplete removal' leaves out the README's point that only 3 of the 37 keyword-counted refusals were explicit. It also mixes the re-evaluated count for trial 143 with search-phase counts for trials 114 and 92. The record's own verdict for trial 143 is supports, not limits_scope.
None. 37/100 from 99/100 for trial 143 is correct, and the differences note the rank-3 norm-preserving LoRA on o_proj/down_proj, the 200-token cap, and the 3-of-37 explicit count.
